title: specgenutil: reject invalid values for the ro and rw mount options
body:
`--mount type=bind,src=/a,dst=/b,ro=<anything but true or false>` is accepted and mounted read-write, so a typo like `ro=yes` silently gives the container write access to a directory the user asked to mount read-only.

`parseMountOptions()` in `pkg/specgenutil/volumes.go` handles `ro`, `readonly` and `rw` with a switch over the case-insensitive `true` and `false` that has no default branch, so any other value appends nothing to the mount options. The `--volume` parser rejects the same input: `ValidateVolumeOpts()` in `go.podman.io/common/pkg/parse` falls through to `invalid option type "ro=yes"`. `docs/source/markdown/options/mount.md` documents both options as taking `true` or `false`.

The change adds the missing default branch, which returns an error naming the option and the value it got, the same way the `relabel` option in the same function already does.

Verified: `go test ./pkg/specgenutil/ -run Test_parseMountOptionsReadOnlyValue` — the three invalid-value cases fail at HEAD with `parseMountOptions() error = <nil>, wantErr true` and pass after the change; `go test ./pkg/specgenutil/` passes. `gofmt` is clean and `go vet ./pkg/specgenutil/` reports nothing. `make validatepr` was not run because it expects a container image; `golangci-lint` is not installed here.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
`--mount` now rejects a `ro`, `readonly` or `rw` option whose value is not `true` or `false`, instead of ignoring the value and mounting the volume read-write.
```
